Even as they continue to pretend that they value freedom, they see someone else do something that offends them, and they insist that that other person should not be allowed to do that.

It's not even that they contradict themselves - that they claim to advocate freedom, then say that other people should not be free. It doesn't even rise to that. Instead, they advocate freedom even as they presume its absence. They don't even start with the notion that other people are or should be free - they start with the presumption of authoritarian constraint - with the unthinking assumption that people are only to be allowed to do some narrow range of things.

If you pay attention, you'll see this presumption over and over.

People will ask, "Should people be allowed to do this?" or "Should it be legal to do that?"

They start with a presumption of the absence of freedom. They don't start with the presumption that people are free to do this or that, and ask if an exception should be made and others should be empowered to deny that freedom. Instead they start with the presumption that the freedom to do the thing does not exist, and ask if it should be extended.

Then they wonder why freedom is so rare and so hard to maintain, and why it's so easy for power-hungry psychopaths to destroy it.

So far just wearing it around the house and doing some jumping, running, bending over, and squatting I have to say I am quite impressed. It seems well put together and I have not felt the gun would come loose or fall out. I don't have a proper belt yet so it sags more than I would like, but that is not the fault of the holster. Following are pictures with a [Sig Sauer SP2022](http://www.sigsauer.com/CatalogProductDetails/sp2022.aspx)

[Covered with my overly large shirt pulled as tightly as possible.](https://i.sli.mg/zKv5Kc.jpg) It is very difficult to see but the grip is noticeable just where the red meets the orange at the middle-right of the picture.

[Uncovered on belt.](https://i.sli.mg/yOuGFy.jpg)

[Sitting on desk you can see the trigger is completely covered.](https://i.sli.mg/TCEZIH.jpg)

[And here you can see how far down the kydex goes as well as the texturing on the holster.](https://i.sli.mg/IcJlXs.jpg)

The tools provided make it extremely easy to adjust the gun position to my liking. I am fine with the standard 15 degree cant it comes with. However I did play around with moving the clips up and down to figure out how high I like it to ride in my pants. This takes all of 15 seconds to do. I figured out the stock configuration is what I prefer.

As for the kydex. It seems solid enough. I did have to loosen it a bit to make holstering and drawing a bit easier. The gun slid in fine but it was a bit too tight to holster when I was wearing it. So I loosened it up and got it working smoothly with just enough retention to hold it in place until I purposefully draw the firearm. I assume when I get a proper belt I will have to readjust the tension.

A word of caution here. The included paperwork recommends blue loctite on all the screws when you finally get everything adjusted perfectly to keep things from loosening up. I won't do this until I have a proper gun belt and have ensured I am happy with the placement of everything. Next on my list is my cwp class next week. Once that's done and I have my license to carry (as it is required in my state) I expect this holster will work wonders. It gets hot here in the south and the material it is made of seems like it would do well with sweat.

[Alien Gear website if you are interested.](http://aliengearholsters.com/)
